### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s).

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f1eeeeeb754fc7bbfe64d89e2a305048a75ac7c`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **60** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f1eeeeeb754fc7bbfe64d89e2a305048a75ac7c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c17d4745c364a07326caa8a359dd182ba1aad10c` — the merge of head `6f6e90033c775667aeb3a6bb20fa88d74f1cfd08` into base `0f1eeeeeb754fc7bbfe64d89e2a305048a75ac7c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c17d4745c364a07326caa8a359dd182ba1aad10c && git checkout c17d4745c364a07326caa8a359dd182ba1aad10c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0f1eeeeeb754fc7bbfe64d89e2a305048a75ac7c 6f6e90033c775667aeb3a6bb20fa88d74f1cfd08 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0f1eeeeeb754fc7bbfe64d89e2a305048a75ac7c && git merge --no-ff 6f6e90033c775667aeb3a6bb20fa88d74f1cfd08

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f1eeeeeb754fc7bbfe64d89e2a305048a75ac7c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0f1eeeeeb754fc7bbfe64d89e2a305048a75ac7c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6f6e90033c775667aeb3a6bb20fa88d74f1cfd08`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts, packages/core/src/security/default-organization.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/default-organization.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/default-organization-invariant.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/ensure-default-organization.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.default-organization.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/suggested-audience-bindings.ts + packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-objects-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization-update-door.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts, .github/workflows/upgrade-harness-optin.yml, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .changeset/24883-last-admin-guard-default-organization-anchor.md, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md (D3, D5, D9, D10), docs/adr/0135-sso-scim-per-environment.md (D5.2). The changeset `.changeset/25208-default-organization-one-definition.md` is judged under ② as prose.

Inputs read: card #25208 (body, claim 6345294692, os-dev-report 6348218751); record 6253205661 on #15212; PR #25265 body and its 13-file list; the net diff `0b8bce40e0..6f6e90033c` (13 files, +516/−117; commits 4be9398455, 40622bd5e7, 2c165f8b8f and the merge 6f6e90033c of `main`); the 46 check-runs on the head. `origin/main` is `284e04810a`, two commits past the merge-base (`0f1eeeeeb7` #25259, `284e04810a` #25258): neither touches any of the 13 paths, so the net diff is current. Check-runs: every completed run on the head concluded `success` or `skipped`; none failed, none pending — Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Test Core (6/6), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, the three single-writer/claim guards, all success. The `18.x upgrade harness (opt-in)` lane has two runs on this head: workflow run 39826380644 (created 17:51:54Z, the pull_request event that fired before `needs:upgrade-harness` landed at 17:51:57Z) concluded `skipped` by the workflow's own label condition, and run 39826393590 (the `labeled` event, created 17:52:00Z, completed 18:00:16Z) concluded `success`. The lane's verdict on this head is success; the skipped twin is the pre-label run, not a measurement.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The `sys_organization` `beforeInsert` guard — right.**
- Registration: `last-admin-guard.ts` registers `guardOrganizationInsert` on `beforeInsert` of `sys_organization`, priority 20, the guard's own `packageId`, beside the update and delete halves. `engine.ts` (16781–16820) dispatches `beforeInsert` once per row of a batch (`dispatch.mode: 'per-row'`), so `ctx.input.data` is one row and the docblock's batch claim holds.
- What it refuses, exactly: on a non-walled posture, an insert that — simulated into both reads of the Default Organization definition — takes `admin_full_access`-anchored platform standing from every unbanned administrator with nobody left (`enforceStanding`: `losing` non-empty AND `unbannedAfter` empty). Under `single` that is: a second organization of any slug beside a sole organization not slugged `default`, or a new organization slugged `default` beside a sole one with another slug — and only when the sole organization's grant holders have no owner/admin membership, no `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` administrator exists, and not every administrator is already banned. Admitted: a `default`-slugged Default Organization that stays put (the slug read still names it), any surviving membership standing, any configured administrator, and every write under a wall.
- The rule under ADR-0131 D5: right. D5 makes the Default Organization's grant the `single` anchor, D3/D5 define that organization by slug else sole-ness, and the ADR's 2026-10-22 D5 note (seat decision 6324268472) says that with no nameable Default Organization no grant anchors — so the resolver's answer can move with no grant touched, which is the fail-open 6253205661 carrier 1 named (and the loss also disarms the guard: `before.size === 0` reads as the bootstrap window; the dev's measurement (A) reproduced exactly that). The guard's charter is ADR-0135 D5.2's break-glass invariant ("an environment may never be left with zero administrators who can sign in"), and the update and delete halves (#24883, #24948) already judge the Default Organization re-slug and delete by that question. The insert half asks the same question with the same enumerate–simulate–enumerate machinery, so the three halves cannot drift. A stricter standing-preservation rule would refuse legitimate growth of a deployment that has another administrator; fixing the anchor by re-slugging a row the caller did not touch would be a write nobody asked for. The refusal's remedy names the two real operator moves (slug the sole organization `default` first, or grant another account standing), and a pin shows the first makes the insert admitted.
- The boundary this leaves, stated by the dev and pinned by the CONTROL "an administrator left standing elsewhere admits the insert": in the common production shape the first administrator is also bound as `owner` of the Default Organization by `ensureDefaultOrganization`, so the insert is admitted and the grant stops anchoring silently — platform standing drops while organization standing remains. That is the same verdict the update half gives a re-slug, consistent with ADR-0135 D5.2, and the BREAKING banner names exactly the narrower population the refusal reaches. Judged right under the ADRs as they stand; recorded in ③ as a design question, not a defect.
- Legitimate inserts, each checked in code: (a) the boot invariant `ensureDefaultOrganizationExists` inserts only when `found.id` is undefined and not `several` — zero organizations. In `AuthPlugin.start()` it runs (line 886) before `registerLastAdminGuard` (line 1695), so a fresh boot's insert is not judged at all; were it judged, zero organizations means no grant anchors, `before` is empty, the inserted row owns no grant, and `refuseIfEmptiedRatherThanFresh` reads dangling grants only through `anchorOwnerTest` with no Default Organization, so it returns as fresh: admitted. (b) `ensureDefaultOrganization`'s `tryInsert` of a `default`-slugged row runs only when no Default Organization is nameable (zero, or several non-default): before it no grant anchors, after it the new row owns none, `losing` is empty: admitted. (c) Seed replay: `seed-loader.ts` writes no `sys_organization` row (it resolves `organization_id` references); an application seed that carries organizations loads after the boot invariant under `single` (D3), so the Default Organization is slugged `default` and stays put: admitted. (d) A walled create: `guardOrganizationInsert` returns on `postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())` before `enforceStanding`; the CONTROL pins zero `engine.find` calls; the dev's R4 drove two `POST /auth/organization/create` through it under `isolated` and `group`. (e) The ceremony creates the organization through the same invariant on a 17.x store that holds none (admitted as in (a)) and attributes rows by raw SQL, never through the engine.
- Simulation verified: an id-less payload is simulated under `INSERTED_ORGANIZATION_ID`, which no grant names; the slug read appends the inserted row and re-filters on slug and non-empty id; the page read keeps `limit + ids.size` and appends the inserted row, so sole-plus-inserted reads as several; `applyPending` leaves stored rows alone (`ids` empty). Fail-closed is kept: the `scan` ceiling and read failures refuse through `failClosed`. The dev's ablations (enforceStanding removed, wall short-circuit removed, inserted row dropped) each red the pins that would catch them.

**2. One Default Organization definition — right; all seven former copies compute the same organization.**
`findDefaultOrganization(read)`: `{ slug: 'default' }` limit 1, else `{}` limit 2 and sole, `idOf` = non-empty string of any id, `several` reported. Checked copy by copy against the removed code:
- resolver `readDefaultOrganizationId`: same `idOf`, same two reads through `tryFind`; kept the `registryHoldsObject` short-circuit and the loud `AuthzStoreUnavailableError`. Same answer; the memo and `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` are untouched.
- `default-organization-invariant.ts`: same reads, propagating; `ambiguous.organizationCount` was `existing.length` under a limit of 2, so it was already always 2 — now the literal, with the reason beside it. Same answer; `several` replaces the former more-than-one length test exactly.
- `ensure-default-organization.ts`: `findDefaultOrganizationId` over swallowing `tryFind`; the walled branch still reads only `slug = 'default'`, and lines 541–549 say why (under a wall an organization is a tenant's boundary, never "the" organization) — justified by ADR-0131 D5 (no grant row under a wall) and D12, unchanged by this PR.
- `last-admin-guard.ts`: the guard's own read with the pending simulation and `scan`; before, `.find(slug === 'default' && toId(id))` then a page of `2 + ids.size` with `length === 1`; now the same through the callback. Kept on purpose and rightly: the resolver's read cannot simulate a pending write and would answer where the guard must refuse.
- `tenancy-service.ts` `resolveDefaultOrgId`: over `findRows` (a thrown read is `[]`), `null` for none. Same answer.
- `suggested-audience-bindings.ts` `resolveDefaultOrganizationId`: over `scopedSystemCtx()` with `fields: ['id']`, a thrown read propagates. Declared edge: a numeric id was read as none and is now read as its string — aligned to the resolver, which the promotion (`bootstrap-platform-admin.ts`, which calls this reader) must agree with so the row it writes is the row the resolver reads. Right.
- `organization-ownership-plan.ts`: raw SQL; a store with no `slug` column answers the slug read `[]`. Declared edge: a `default`-slugged row with a blank id used to name nothing and now falls through to the sole reading — the resolver's reading, which D10 fate 3 must match for the certified database to boot. Right.
The core test pins the rule (slug wins without a second read; sole; several; none; blank id; propagation) and the resolver's read over it (registry absent is not read).

**3. The ceremony pin — right, as carrier 2 asked.** `grant_promoted` (NULL `organization_id`, by id to a NULL-owned `admin_full_access` mirror — the 17.x shape) is in the acceptance fixture; the test reads `readDefaultOrganizationId` from `@objectstack/core` over the same SQLite database (a one-argument `find` double; `registryHoldsObject` reads no registry as held) before the ceremony and pins the attributed owner equal to that answer (`org_default`, the `default`-slugged row beside `org_b`), and NULL under a wall. The fixture consequences are right: the catalog double declares `admin_full_access` as the composed security plugin ships it; the "uncomposed security plugin" block opts out, which is its premise; the walled `sys_permission_set` count 3 → 4 is the extra mirror a wall does not delete. The dev's ablation note is honest (a plan naming `org_b` reds the file at the effective-access assertion before the new pin); the pin still binds the ceremony to the resolver's answer.

**4. Published surface of `@objectstack/core`.** New on the root index (via `export * from './security/index.js'`): `readDefaultOrganizationId` (was private), `findDefaultOrganization`, `DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION_SLUG`, and the types `DefaultOrganizationRead` and `DefaultOrganizationAnswer`. Additive, named right, with the read-policy contract in the docblocks. Callers on the head: plugin-auth (invariant, bootstrap, tenancy, guard), plugin-security (bindings), cli (plan; apply test). plugin-auth, plugin-security and cli publish no new symbol.

**5. The dev's residual — `default`-slug capture under `single`.** Reach, read in code: at insert time a new organization owns no grant, so capture needs a later `admin_full_access` grant owned by it (a platform-level writer's act) or an existing organization re-slugged to `default` (the update half's domain, pre-existing). Doors to the insert under `single`: better-auth `POST /auth/organization/create` answers 403 `ORGANIZATION_CREATION_DISABLED` (`auth-manager.ts` 3712–3720, `multiOrgPostureEffective()`); the data API declares `apiMethods: ['get', 'list', 'update']` on `sys_organization`, so `create` is 405, and the `import` the 405 body advertises is gated precisely by write mode (`data-action-routes.ts` 388/498 → `api-derivation.ts` 364–368): insert-mode and upsert-mode need `create` and are 405 before the engine; only update-mode import is admitted, which is an engine update. So the half guards writers below HTTP — seeds, scripts, a host's engine calls — as the PR says. Severity: low; the admitted capture is bounded by needing a platform-level writer, and the lockout and the disarmed guard are closed. The open door is the update half's slug (③).

**6. R1–R4.** R1 (a fresh install boots and serves under `single`): the dev measured a production `os serve` of `examples/app-crm` on a fresh SQLite (health, sign-up, sign-in, session 200) and the harness's fresh-store leg passed in CI. R2 (HEAD refuses the 18.0 fixture until the ceremony, then boots it) and R3 (a v17-shaped store is refused, takes the ceremony, boots): the labelled harness lane concluded success on this head (run 39826393590). R4 (walled postures boot and serve with no organization-less grant): the dev measured `isolated` and `group`, two organization creates each through the hook's wall path, 0 organization-less grants. Nothing in the diff touches a boot refusal, the ceremony's step order or DDL, so the CI legs are the right evidence to rely on.

### ② Semver level
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset: right — the engine's `sys_organization` insert accept-set narrows under `single`. No widening arm is owed by the core exports: clause ② is the payload accept-set, and the level reads the kind.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. No authorable key is added, removed, tombstoned or re-meant; the change is a runtime refusal plus TS exports (the kind table in `pr-automation.yml` and AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 on `main`: non-authorable internal types, services, `fix!:` alike → `patch`).
- Levels `patch` on `core`, `plugin-auth`, `plugin-security`, `cli`: right under maintainer ruling A of 2026-10-21 (#25105): the level follows the kind alone, `none` takes `patch` on every entry (a `minor` would be refused as `none-minor` by `check-changeset-no-major`'s level axis), and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its carriers. Record 6253205661's "a `minor` widening of core, declared then" predates ruling A and is superseded by it; `.changeset/24883-last-admin-guard-default-organization-anchor.md` (a narrowing at `patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`) is the landed precedent.
- Carriers: `!` on the title; the BREAKING banner names the exact population (a `single` deployment whose only organization is not slugged `default` and whose last administrator holds only its grant), FROM/TO per item, and the operator action. The ADR-0087 marker is exactly one, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why — a category in `CATEGORIES`, honest because no metadata key moves, `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and no tombstone is owed; the body's operator action is a data remedy, not a consumer code rewrite, so the prescription detector has nothing to refuse. The real gate ran on this head (`Check Changeset` runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base` after its self-test) and concluded success, as did the level axis.
- `check-governed-merges`: 0 of 13 paths governed; not Tier H or S — consistent with the file list (no `docs/adr/**`, no spec schema).

### ③ Boundary flags
- os-dev-report: `premise_still_valid: true`; `open_questions: []`; three out-of-scope findings, three deviations, one not-measured note — each answered below.
- Finding 1 (class a: `default`-slug anchor capture admitted when another administrator stands): judged in ① item 5 — bounded at the insert. The real capture door is a RE-SLUG of an existing organization to `default` through the update half: better-auth `organization/update` accepts `slug` (`sys-organization-update-door.test.ts` line 83), its `beforeUpdateOrganization` (`auth-manager.ts` 3859) checks only the environment binding, and the `single` gate at 3712 is on create alone; the data door's user-context PATCH of better-auth's own columns is refused by ADR-0092 D2 per the object's note. On a multi-organization `single` store with no `default` slug — the shape the boot already warns about — an organization owner whose organization holds a platform-granted `admin_full_access` can become platform administrator by re-slugging it. Pre-existing, outside this card's surface, measured by nobody. ESCALATE: a card under #15212's reconciliation to measure the better-auth `organization/update` slug door under `single` and decide whether the update half refuses a re-slug TO `default` beside other organizations, or whether `multiOrgPostureEffective()` gates the slug too. Not a FAIL here: this PR does not open it.
- Finding 2 (the anchor predicate spelled twice — `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` in core, `anchorOwnerTest` in the guard): accurate, and the dev's reason not to fold them holds (the guard's form reads the simulated Default Organization). It is the half of 6253205661 carrier 3 that claim 6345294692 left out. ESCALATE: record it in the epic's reconciliation ledger so it is not lost a second time; exporting `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` is its own card (a `none`-kind `patch` widening of core).
- Finding 3 (`ambiguous.organizationCount` is always 2; `auth-plugin.ts` 890, `identity-objects-plugin.ts` 132 and `cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts` 1010 print "holds 2 organizations"): pre-existing, now explicit in code. Accept as cosmetic; a follow-up may print "several" instead. No action owed here.
- "Not measured: whether `import` on `sys_organization` reaches `beforeInsert`": answered by reading in ① item 5 — insert-mode and upsert-mode imports are refused 405 before the engine by the precise write-mode gate; no insert reaches the hook from that door; update-mode import is the update half's.
- Design question, not escalated as a defect: the insert half admits the move whenever any administrator (an organization owner included) remains, so platform standing can still drop silently in the owner-bound shape. That is ADR-0135 D5.2's invariant as the update and delete halves already apply it; a standing-preservation rule for the D5 anchor would be a new decision for the epic seat, not this card.
- Deviation 1 (worktree moved to `../objectstack-issue-25208` after the main-checkout hook refused writes): process only; branch and remote are the claim's. Deviation 2 (trailer pair in the AGENTS.md form, not the harness-suggested model-named one): AGENTS.md wins, as the harness reminder itself says. Deviation 3 (catalog double declares `admin_full_access` by default; the uncomposed block opts out; walled count 3 → 4): judged right in ① item 3.
- Claim scope held: no `docs/adr/**`, no `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_SHAPE_GENERATION` change, the localization fallback in `resolve-authz-context.ts` untouched (the diff there is one function and one import).
- The two gates the dev could not run locally (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) are covered by `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Build Core` on the head, both success. The PR is still a draft; this record does not change that.

Seat ACCEPT · epic PM `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-22T18:51Z. PR #25265 at `6f6e90033c775667aeb3a6bb20fa88d74f1cfd08` (#25208; claim 6345294692; os-dev-report 6348218751). **ACCEPT.**

## Seat check

- **Shape:** 13 files, +516 / −117. `check-governed-merges --pr 25265`: 0 of 13 paths governed, so this is an ordinary queue landing.
- **What it does:** the three 8c-2 review carriers (6253205661).
  - **Carrier 1, a new `sys_organization` `beforeInsert` guard.** It refuses an insert under `single` that would leave no administrator who can sign in. The dev measured that a second organization beside a sole non-`default` one can end the admin's standing. The guard uses the same enumerate–simulate–enumerate rule as the update and delete halves (ADR-0135 D5.2), and does no reads under a wall.
  - **Carrier 2, the ceremony pin.** A NULL `admin_full_access` grant is attributed to `readDefaultOrganizationId`'s answer.
  - **Carrier 3, one Default Organization definition** exported from core (`findDefaultOrganization`, `DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION_SLUG`, `readDefaultOrganizationId`). The seven former copies compute the same organization and keep only their own read policy.
- **Review:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, narrowing face, from an isolated reviewer: **PASS** at this head (the record above).
  - Every legitimate insert is admitted, judged by reading the code: the boot invariant, `ensureDefaultOrganization`, seed replay, a walled create, the ceremony.
  - The changeset is right: all `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, BREAKING, and ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- **CI:** the latest run of every check is success or skipped. The labelled `18.x upgrade harness` lane passed (run 39826393590); its skipped twin is the pre-label run.
- **R1–R4:**
  - R2 and R3 are the harness lane.
  - R1 and R4 were measured by the dev on this head: a production `os serve` under `single`, `isolated` and `group` each answered 200; two walled organization creates each passed through the guard's wall path; 0 organization-less grants.
  - Full dogfood passed 2481/2481.
- **Escalations, and where each goes:**
  - **Security, filed as its own card under #15212:** under `single`, an existing organization can be re-slugged to `default` through better-auth `organization/update`. The `single` gate in `auth-manager.ts` covers create only, and `beforeUpdateOrganization` checks only the environment-binding slug lock. That re-slug moves the platform-admin anchor; this PR does not open it.
